basic_identification.full_title: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services — Part 1 Safety Requirements (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Electrotechnical (approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Lamps and Related Equipment Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies safety and interchangeability requirements, together with the test methods and conditions, for self-ballasted LED lamps with integrated means for stable operation intended for domestic and similar general lighting purposes. It applies to lamps with a rated power up to 60 W, a rated AC voltage above 50 V up to 250 V (at 50 Hz), a DC voltage up to 1 000 V, and possessing Edison screw (E14, E27) or Bayonet (B15d, B22d) caps. It also covers photobiological safety, lamps incorporating rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, and lamps with auxiliary functions such as sensors, communication technologies, or speakers.

certification_and_marking.disclaimer: No mandatory BIS product certification (such as the ISI Mark or CRS Registration) is strictly required within the code of practice text itself for finished, erected systems or sales. However, to guarantee quality and consumer safety, the standard establishes the voluntary BIS Standard Mark scheme alongside critical material-level, warning, and test certification requirements:

requirements.provision: The LED lamp(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, and marked with the Standard Mark.

Lamps must be clearly and legibly marked with the trade-mark, rated voltage, rated power, and rated frequency. Legibility is checked by rubbing lightly for 15 s with a cloth soaked in water, followed by 15 s with a cloth soaked in hexane.

Lamps that are not suitable for direct water contact must be clearly marked with the 'Not suitable for use under moisture' graphical symbol (minimum 5 mm height) on the packaging or bear a caution note: 'Use in Dry Locations only'.
Non-dimmable lamps must be marked with a standardized 'dimming not allowed' symbol on the lamp package.
If a lamp has operating position limitations (due to potential overheating), a designated warning symbol must be printed on the lamp, with adjacent text to prevent reading it upside down.
Compliance with photobiological eye safety must be certified, classifying the lamp as either Risk Group 0 (unlimited) or Risk Group 1 (unlimited) in accordance with IS 16661.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2026 is the core national safety specification in India for self-ballasted LED lamps utilized in domestic and similar general lighting networks. It defines safety constraints for lamps up to 60 W operating at AC voltages between 50 V and 250 V. This first revision introduces strict checks for abnormal operations, ingress protection (IP ratings), photobiological hazards (specifically blue light evaluation classifying products into safe Risk Groups RG0 or RG1), and safety rules for integrated lithium-ion batteries. When verifying safety compliance, engineers must check that the lamp caps conform to mechanical gauges (E14, E27, B15d, or B22d) and that all insulating components holding live electrical parts in place withstand the ball-pressure test at a minimum of 125 °C and the glow-wire test at 650 °C.
